name: Pentetrazol
summary: Pentylenetetrazol (PTZ), or pentylenetetrazole, also known as pentetrazol (INNTooltip International Nonproprietary Name) and sold under the brand name Metrazol, is a drug formerly used as a circulatory and respiratory stimulant. High doses cause convulsions, as discovered by Hungarian-American neurologist and psychiatrist Ladislas J. Meduna in 1934.

pharmacology.text: The mechanism of pentylenetetrazol is not well-understood, and it may have multiple actions. In 1984, Squires et al. published a report analyzing pentylenetetrazol and several structurally related convulsant drugs. They found that in-vivo convulsant potency was strongly correlated to in-vitro affinity to the picrotoxin binding site on the GABAA receptor.
pharmacology.kind: GABAA receptor antagonist; Convulsant; Anxiogenic; Stimulant; Wakefulness-promoting agent

uses.text: Pentylenetetrazol (PTZ), or pentylenetetrazole, also known as pentetrazol (INN) and sold under the brand name Metrazol, is a drug formerly used as a circulatory and respiratory stimulant. It has been used in convulsive therapy, and was found to be effective in treating depression, but side effects, such as uncontrolled seizures, were difficult to avoid.

sideEffects.text: Pentylenetetrazol is anxiogenic and has been known to induce severe anxiety in humans.

fact.en: Sold as Metrazol, it was used in the 1930s to bring on convulsions deliberately as a treatment for mental illness, before electroconvulsive therapy replaced it. Today it is used in the laboratory to test anticonvulsant drugs.
fact.zh: 它以 Metrazol 的商品名販售，在 1930 年代被用來刻意誘發抽搐以治療精神疾病，後來被電痙攣療法取代。如今它用於實驗室測試抗癲癇藥物。
fact.zhHans: 它以 Metrazol 的商品名贩售，在 1930 年代被用来刻意诱发抽搐以治疗精神疾病，后来被电痉挛疗法取代。如今它用于实验室测试抗癫痫药物。
